title: Comment on long-term outcomes of bone-anchored maxillary protraction in patients with unilateral complete cleft lip and palate
html: We read with great interest the prospective study titled “Orthognathic surgery need following BAMP therapy in unilateral complete cleft lip and palate with moderate to severe maxillary deficiency: a prospective study” by Petruccelli et al.1 The study addresses an important and underexplored question regarding the long-term stability of bone-anchored maxillary protraction (BAMP) and its potential to reduce surgical intervention. As one of the first prospective longitudinal investigations to follow patients until the completion of facial growth, it provides valuable long-term evidence, with nearly half of the patients avoiding surgery.
